summary: Dorchester County tower built 1932 at 120 ft, dismantled 2018, restored to 40 ft and re-erected at the Church Creek Forestry office; FFLA's relocation label is not supported.

facts.design: 120-foot Aermotor tower with 7 by 7 ft metal cab and rooftop catwalk (NHLR)

access.note: Small park with interpretive panels and accessible parking off Golden Hill Road; the tower itself is not open for climbing

events.note: Built by the Maryland Forest Service (NHLR); November 1932 report describes a new 120-ft steel tower about two miles south of Church Creek
Decommissioned circa 1978 as fire detection technology advanced; then stood idle
Dismantled due to deteriorating and unsafe conditions; DNR kept the top 40 ft including the cab
Top 40 ft restored and re-erected at the forestry field office; NHLR says work was complete as of 2024

corrections.current: relocated: Moved from Church Creek to the Church Creek Display
corrections.proposed: Remove the relocated event; add removed (2018, dismantled) and restored (2024, top 40 ft re-erected at the forestry field office)
corrections.why: DNR's report lists Brandywine, Great Mills, Hollofield and Quantico as moved and does not list Church Creek; the engineering firm says the tower was dismantled in 2018 and re-erected at 4329 Golden Hill Road.

corrections.proposed: 38.62328, -76.13468 (NHLR coordinates for the Church Creek Forestry station)
corrections.why: NHLR places the tower at the Church Creek Forestry station and the engineering firm gives that station's address as 4329 Golden Hill Road. FFLA's display point is nearly identical to its own 'Tower Gone' entry for the original site, so it does not mark a different place.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLA calls the display a relocated Church Creek tower. DNR's report does not list the tower among moved towers, and the engineering firm describes dismantling and re-erection at the forestry field office. The relocation is treated as unsupported and the 2018 removal and 2024 restoration are recorded instead.

NHLR gives both 100 ft and 120 ft for the tower. The 1932 report and the engineering firm give 120 ft as built. Current height is 40 ft per NHLR and the engineering firm, so height_m is set to the current 12.2 m.

notes_for_editor: Parent record data/towers/md/us-md-church-creek-forestry.json carries the same 'relocated' event and the NHLR coordinates (38.62328, -76.13468); the same correction should be applied there. FFLA's own coordinates for the original Church Creek entry (38.47420, -76.14273, Tower Gone) and the display (38.47420, -76.14248) are almost identical, so FFLA's point may simply be wrong; confirm the station coordinates before publishing the location change. NHLR says 'As of 2024' for the reduction, while the engineering firm's entry form says the project was substantially completed between November 1, 2022 and October 31, 2024. The DNR report is marked DRAFT. Access is rated public on the basis of the engineering firm's description of the park and parking; no visiting hours were found and NHLR says the tower is not open for climbing. The DNR history page linked from NHLR was not read.
